name: afs_create_yfs_cm_token
prose: Real function afs_create_yfs_cm_token(challenge, server) in fs/afs/cm_security.c (slice cuts the head). Precondition: server is a valid afs_server whose cell->net is valid; challenge is the received rxrpc challenge skb. Postcondition: returns -ENOKEY if net->fs_cm_token_key is NULL; -ENOPKG if no krb5 enctype matches rxgk_kernel_query_challenge(challenge); -ENOMEM if the appdata buffer allocation (kzalloc) fails; the negative error from crypto_krb5_prepare_encryption (PTR_ERR of the aead) if that fails; or the negative error from crypto_krb5_encrypt if encrypting the token fails. Otherwise it builds the XDR appdata (initiator and acceptor UUIDs, capability list, connection enctype, a fresh random callback key K0, and a token container whose encrypted token holds K0, level ENCRYPT, zero times and one identity with the server UUID), encrypts the token in place, stores adatasize and the appdata pointer into server->cm_rxgk_appdata (ownership of the buffer passes to the server) and returns the non-negative result of crypto_krb5_encrypt (0 on success). The aead handle is always freed; on every failure path the appdata buffer is kfree'd and server->cm_rxgk_appdata is left unchanged. A size mismatch between the built layout and adatasize only logs pr_err and does not abort.

name: afs_read_dir
prose: Precondition: dvnode is an AFS directory vnode; file is the file through which the synchronous read may be done; the caller holds no dvnode->validate_lock. Postcondition: on success (return value >= 0) the function returns with dvnode->validate_lock held for reading (taken by down_read_killable if AFS_VNODE_DIR_VALID and AFS_VNODE_DIR_READ were both already set, in which case the return value is the i_size sampled on entry; otherwise taken by downgrade_write after the write lock was acquired) and the caller must up_read it. After a successful return AFS_VNODE_DIR_VALID and AFS_VNODE_DIR_READ are both set. If the write lock was obtained and the flags turned out valid (checked under the write lock) the return value is the i_size sampled on entry; if a reload was needed (afs_invalidate_cache(dvnode,0) is called first when DIR_VALID is clear) the return value is that of afs_read_single, i.e. the number of bytes read, which is at least the current i_size (it may differ from the entry-time i_size). On failure it returns a negative errno with no lock held: -ERESTARTSYS if either killable lock wait is interrupted (when the write lock wait fails the read lock was already released), -ESTALE if the directory grew while being read (caller must call again), the error from afs_dir_check, or the error from the netfs single read; in the read-failure cases the write lock is released with up_write and the DIR flags are not set by this call.

name: afs_edit_dir_add
prose: Precondition: the caller holds the directory inode lock; vnode is a directory vnode; name is the entry name (name->name NUL terminated, length name->len) and new_fid is the fid of the new entry; why is the trace reason. Postcondition: returns nothing. If i_size exceeds AFS_DIR_BLOCK_SIZE * AFS_DIR_MAX_BLOCKS or is not a multiple of AFS_DIR_BLOCK_SIZE, afs_invalidate_dir(afs_dir_invalid_edit_add_bad_size) is called and nothing is edited. If block 0 cannot be mapped, returns with no change. If i_size == 0 the directory is initialised: block 0 is initialised as meta block, i_size is set to AFS_DIR_BLOCK_SIZE, and the entry is placed at slot AFS_DIR_RESV_BLOCKS0 of block 0. Otherwise blocks 0..nr_blocks (one beyond the last) are scanned (skipping blocks below AFS_DIR_BLOCKS_WITH_CTR whose allocation counter is smaller than the slots needed) for a run of afs_dir_calc_slots(name->len) contiguous free slots; a new block b == nr_blocks is initialised and i_size grown to (b+1)*AFS_DIR_BLOCK_SIZE before searching it. If nr_blocks >= AFS_DIR_MAX_BLOCKS the directory is invalidated (afs_dir_invalid_edit_add_too_many_blocks) and the error trace is emitted; if a block cannot be mapped the error trace is emitted; if AFS_VNODE_DIR_VALID is clear when a block is mapped the edit is abandoned with the create_inval trace; if no block has space the nospc trace is emitted and the directory is invalidated (afs_dir_invalid_edit_add_no_slots). On success the dirent (valid=1, vnode, unique, name copy, NUL) is written, the slots are marked in the block bitmap, the allocation counter of the block is reduced when the block is below AFS_DIR_BLOCKS_WITH_CTR, the entry is linked at the head of its hash bucket in the meta block, the inode i_version is incremented, the n_dir_cr stat is counted and the inode is marked dirty. All mapped blocks (block and meta) are unmapped on every return path; no lock, reference or memory is acquired or retained.

name: afs_silly_iput
prose: Precondition: dentry is a dentry of an AFS file with a valid parent directory dentry, inode is the AFS inode being released, dvnode->silly_key is a valid key and the caller does not hold dvnode->rmdir_lock. Postcondition: takes dvnode->rmdir_lock for reading and releases it on every return path. Returns 0 (no other effect) if d_alloc_parallel on the parent fails with an error. If d_alloc_parallel returns a dentry that is not in lookup (race with lookup): under alias->d_lock, if the alias is positive and DCACHE_NFSFS_RENAMED is not set the flag is set and 1 is returned, otherwise 0 is returned; the alias reference is dropped (dput) in both cases. Otherwise (alias in lookup): vnode->lock_state is set to AFS_VNODE_LOCK_DELETED under vnode->lock, afs_do_silly_unlink(dvnode, vnode, dentry, dvnode->silly_key) is called (its result is ignored), d_lookup_done(alias) and dput(alias) are done and 1 is returned. The caller's references to dentry and inode are not consumed.

name: afs_lock_work
prose: Precondition: work is the lock_work.work delayed-work item embedded in a live afs_vnode, run from the lock manager workqueue, and the caller does not hold vnode->lock. Postcondition: returns nothing and never returns with vnode->lock held. It takes vnode->lock and dispatches on vnode->lock_state (the GRANTED case can jump back to re-dispatch after the state changed while the lock was dropped). NEED_UNLOCK: sets UNLOCKING, drops the spinlock, calls afs_release_lock(vnode, vnode->lock_key) (a failure other than when the state became DELETED is traced and logged), retakes the spinlock, then calls afs_kill_lockers_enoent if the result was -ENOENT, else afs_next_locker(vnode, 0), unlocks and returns. GRANTED: asserts granted_locks is non-empty, takes a reference on lock_key, sets EXTENDING, drops the spinlock, calls afs_extend_lock, puts the key reference, logs on error, retakes the spinlock; on -ENOENT kills the lockers with -ENOENT, unlocks and returns; if the state is no longer EXTENDING it re-dispatches; otherwise it sets the state back to GRANTED, requeues lock_work after HZ*10 if ret != 0 (any other error), unlocks and returns. WAITING_FOR_CB: calls afs_next_locker(vnode, 0), unlocks, returns. DELETED: kills the lockers with -ENOENT, unlocks, returns. Any other state: unlocks and returns without action. Key references taken are always released.

name: afs_do_setlk
prose: Precondition: file is an open AFS file whose inode maps to a live afs_vnode, fl is a lock request not yet linked on any vnode list, the caller holds no vnode->lock. Postcondition: initialises fl->fl_ops, the fl_u.afs link and state AFS_LOCK_PENDING and returns, after possibly sleeping, one of: 0 if the lock was granted and registered with the VFS (locks_lock_file_wait succeeded) and afs_validate was called (its error ignored); for server-backed locks fl is then on vnode->granted_locks with state AFS_LOCK_GRANTED; for flock mode local or a partial-file lock in openafs mode no server lock is taken (fl is not put on any vnode list). A negative errno from afs_validate or afs_check_permit, or -EACCES if the key lacks the required rights (nothing queued). -ENOENT if vnode->lock_state is AFS_VNODE_LOCK_DELETED (fl is left on pending_locks). -EAGAIN if the request is non-blocking (no FL_SLEEP) and the file is locked by someone else, or the server says would-block (fl removed from pending_locks, next locker woken). If the server RPC fails: permission errors (-EKEY*, -EPERM, -EACCES), -ENOENT or other errors are returned after storing them in fl->fl_u.afs.state, unlinking fl and passing the lock to the next locker (or killing lockers on -ENOENT). If a blocking request must wait, it sleeps interruptibly until fl state leaves AFS_LOCK_PENDING: a signal returns -ERESTARTSYS (fl is left pending), a state of YOUR_TRY retries the server request, GRANTED completes, and a negative state is returned as the error. If locks_lock_file_wait fails its negative errno is returned and, for server-backed locks, fl is unlinked and afs_defer_unlock queues release of the server lock. The function never returns -EINPROGRESS; vnode->lock is not held on return. It may set vnode->lock_key (key reference taken), lock_type and lock_state SETTING/WAITING_FOR_CB and queue lock_work after HZ*5 while waiting.

name: afs_fileserver_probe_result
prose: Precondition: call is a completed FS.GetCapabilities probe call with call->probe a live endpoint state whose address list has an entry at call->probe_index, call->server the probed server, call->net valid, and estate->nr_probing >= 1; the caller holds no server->probe_lock. Postcondition: returns nothing. It stores call->error in the addressed address's last_error, then under server->probe_lock classifies the result. error 0: estate->error = 0 and the address is marked as responded. error -ECONNABORTED: marked as responded too and, unless the estate already has AFS_ESTATE_RESPONDED, estate->abort_code = call->abort_code and estate->error = -ECONNABORTED. 'Marked as responded' means: the failed_set bit is cleared; the YFS flags (ESTATE_IS_YFS and server IS_YFS and service_id when call->service_id == YFS_FS_SERVICE, else ESTATE_NOT_YFS and, if the estate is not YFS, server IS_YFS cleared, service_id set, and server HAS_FS64 set or cleared from the capability word call->tmp) are updated; estate->rtt, server->rtt and alist->preferred are set to the new srtt when it is smaller than estate->rtt; then AFS_ESTATE_RESPONDED, the responsive_set bit and server AFS_SERVER_FL_RESPONDING are set. error -ENOMEM or -ENONET: the responsive_set bit is cleared and AFS_ESTATE_LOCAL_FAILURE is set; failed_set and estate->error are not changed. Any other error (including -ECONNRESET, -ERFKILL, -EADDRNOTAVAIL, -ENETUNREACH, -EHOSTUNREACH, -EHOSTDOWN, -ECONNREFUSED, -ETIMEDOUT, -ETIME): the responsive bit is cleared, the failed_set bit is set, and estate->error = call->error only if the estate has not responded and estate->error is 0, -ETIMEDOUT or -ETIME. In every case the lock is released, the probe is traced and then afs_done_one_fs_probe runs: estate->nr_probing is decremented, when it reaches 0 the probe set is finished (if the estate responded the server goes on the slow probe list, else server->rtt = UINT_MAX, SERVER_FL_RESPONDING is cleared and the server goes on the fast list; a follow-up probe timer is scheduled), and server->probe_wq is woken (on every call, whether or not nr_probing reached 0). No reference is taken or released.

name: afs_fetch_status
prose: Precondition: vnode is a live AFS vnode with volume set; key is the caller's key (may be NULL); _caller_access is NULL or points to a writable afs_access_t. Postcondition: if afs_alloc_operation fails the function returns its negative errno (PTR_ERR) and *_caller_access is not written. Otherwise it runs a synchronous fetch-status operation on the vnode (afs_fetch_status_operation, one file), then, if _caller_access is non-NULL, stores op->file[0].scb.status.caller_access in *_caller_access (whether or not the operation succeeded), and returns afs_put_operation(op): 0 on success or the negative errno recorded by the operation. On success the vnode's status and callback are updated (afs_fetch_status_success: for a new inode via afs_inode_init_from_status, otherwise afs_vnode_commit_status). The operation is freed before return; no reference or lock is held by the caller afterwards. The is_new argument is not used by the body.

name: afs_iget5_test
prose: Precondition: inode is a valid AFS inode (AFS_FS_I(inode) is its afs_vnode) and opaque points to a struct afs_vnode_param whose fid is initialised. Postcondition: returns 1 if the fid in opaque matches the inode's vnode fid on vnode, vnode_hi and unique (the volume id is not compared), and 0 otherwise; no memory, lock or reference is modified.

name: afs_setattr
prose: Precondition: idmap, dentry (an AFS inode's dentry) and attr are valid; the caller does not hold vnode->validate_lock. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately, changing nothing, if attr->ia_valid has none of the supported attribute bits (SIZE, MODE, UID, GID, MTIME, MTIME_SET, TIMES_SET, TOUCH). If ATTR_SIZE is set: returns -EISDIR if the inode is not a regular file, returns the error from inode_newsize_ok if non-zero, and clears ATTR_SIZE from attr->ia_valid when the new size equals the current i_size. Otherwise it takes an fscache cookie use and the write lock on vnode->validate_lock. For a regular file with ATTR_SIZE it waits for writeback in the range between old and new size (a negative result is returned); if no supported attribute other than size/mtime is requested, the size is shrinking and the new size is above netfs.remote_i_size, the change is applied locally only (truncate_setsize, netfs_resize_file, fscache_resize_cookie) and 0 is returned without contacting the server. Otherwise it allocates an operation (failure: PTR_ERR returned), sets the attribute fields (a size change adds dv_delta 1 and set_size), and returns the result of afs_do_sync_operation (0 or the negative server/network errno). On every path after the lock is taken, the write lock is released and the fscache cookie use is dropped before returning; the early returns (unsupported, -EISDIR, newsize error) happen before the lock and cookie are taken.

name: afs_select_fileserver
prose: Real function bool afs_select_fileserver(op) in fs/afs/rotate.c (slice covers only the middle: abort-code handling, restart and server/address selection); the function head is not in the slice. Precondition: op is an initialised AFS operation with op->volume and op->file[0].vnode set; op->call_error and op->call_abort_code hold the result of the previous attempt (if op->nr_iterations was non-zero); called repeatedly, single-threaded per op. Postcondition: increments op->nr_iterations and returns true if the caller should (re)issue the call: op->server, op->server_index, op->estate and op->addr_index select a responsive server address (marked in op->addr_tried), the volsync times are reset to TIME64_MIN and op->call_responded is false; vnode->cb_server and its callback promise are reset if the chosen server changed. Returns false if the operation is finished: op->flags has AFS_OPERATION_STOP and op->estate is NULL, and the final error is in the op's error (-ENOMEDIUM for a deleted volume, errors accumulated from the probes, -EREMOTEIO, -ETIMEDOUT, -EADV, -EBUSY, -ENOSPC, -EDQUOT, -ENOTSUPP, -ERESTARTSYS, a local error or the volume status error; call_error 0 or a local error simply stops with that error recorded, after clearing the volume offline/busy flags and possibly asking to restart when the volume state needs an update). If the previous call aborted (-ECONNABORTED) the abort code decides whether to try the next server, retry the same server after sleeping for 1s (only for operations restricted to the current server), restart from the volume status check, set flags such as VNOVOL, VBUSY or VMOVED, or fail; on address failures (-ETIMEDOUT, -ETIME, -ECONNREFUSED, ...) it tries the next address; -ECONNRESET/-ENETRESET stop with that error. Side effects: sets/clears server-entry flags AFS_SE_VOLUME_OFFLINE/BUSY, takes the volume servers_lock for writing briefly (VNOVOL) and rcu read locks, may sleep (msleep, probe waits, afs_check_volume_status), and on a restart drops the op's server list reference and clears the server states; it holds no lock on return.

name: afs_deliver_to_call
prose: Precondition: call is a valid, initialised afs_call with call->type->deliver set. Postcondition: returns nothing; the body runs at most one pass. If call->state is not one of AFS_CALL_CL_AWAIT_REPLY, SV_AWAIT_OP_ID, SV_AWAIT_REQUEST, SV_AWAIT_ACK, only call->type->done (if non-NULL) is invoked. In state SV_AWAIT_ACK, rxrpc_kernel_recv_data is called: -EINPROGRESS, -EAGAIN or 0 return with nothing else done; a negative value or 1 (treated as 0) completes the call via afs_set_call_complete(call, ret, remote_abort) and then calls type->done. Otherwise call->type->deliver(call) is called and a 0 return with call->unmarshalling_error becomes -EBADMSG. 0: call->responded is set, afs_queue_call_work is called, and if the state is AFS_CALL_CL_PROC_REPLY the server gets AFS_SERVER_FL_MAY_HAVE_CB (if call->op) and the call is completed with 0, otherwise (state past PROC_REPLY) it is not completed here; type->done is called in both cases. -EINPROGRESS/-EAGAIN: returns, call not completed, done not called. -ECONNABORTED: (call state is already COMPLETE) responded is set and the error logged, done is called, afs_set_call_complete is not called. -ENOTSUPP: responded set, the rxrpc call is aborted with RXGEN_OPCODE, the call is completed with -ENOTSUPP and done is called. -EIO (also logged), -ENODATA, -EBADMSG, -EMSGSIZE, -ENOMEM, -EFAULT: aborted with RXGEN_CC_UNMARSHAL (RXGEN_SS_UNMARSHAL if the state is not CL_AWAIT_REPLY), completed with that error, then done is called. Any other error: aborted with RX_CALL_DEAD, completed with the error, then done is called. No lock or reference is acquired or released here.

name: afs_fs_init
prose: Precondition: called once at module init (__init) with the afs inode cache not yet created and the afs filesystem type not yet registered. Postcondition: sets afs_count_active_inodes to 0 and creates the afs_inode_cache kmem cache (size of struct afs_vnode, HWCACHE_ALIGN|ACCOUNT, constructor afs_i_init_once). If cache creation fails it logs a notice and returns -ENOMEM with the filesystem unregistered. Otherwise it calls register_filesystem(&afs_fs_type); if that returns a negative errno the cache is destroyed (kmem_cache_destroy) and that errno is returned (afs_inode_cachep is not reset to NULL and the filesystem is not registered). On success it returns 0 with the inode cache existing and the filesystem registered. No lock is held and no other resource is left allocated.

name: afs_update_volume_creation_time
prose: Precondition: op is a valid afs_operation whose pre_volsync.creation (old) and volsync.creation (new) hold the creation times before and after the operation; volume is a valid afs_volume; the caller holds no lock this function takes. Postcondition: returns 0 and sets volume->creation_time = new, without anything else, if volume->creation_time was TIME64_MIN; returns 0 changing nothing if new equals the current creation_time or if the current creation_time differs from old (another operation already advanced it). Otherwise (cur == old and new != cur): for an RW volume, and for a Backup volume when new < old, it does atomic_inc(&volume->cb_scrub), emits the creation-regress trace, sets volume->creation_time = new and returns 0 (for an RW volume any change scrubs). For a Backup volume with new >= old, and for an RO volume that passes the exclusion test, it does atomic_inc_return(&volume->cb_ro_snapshot), emits the vos-release trace, sets volume->creation_time = new and returns 0. For an RO volume it first calls afs_is_server_excluded(op, volume): a negative errno from that is returned with nothing changed; a positive value (1, the server is excluded from the volume's server list, possibly after setting AFS_VOLUME_NEEDS_UPDATE and refreshing the volume status) is returned with only the volume-excluded trace emitted and creation_time unchanged. No lock or reference is left held. Increments are plain atomic increments (not a cmpxchg); the guard against races is the cur == old test.

name: afs_extract_vlserver_list
prose: Real function afs_extract_vlserver_list(cell, buffer, buffer_size) in fs/afs/vl_list.c (slice starts mid-function, so the name is not in the slice). Precondition: cell is a valid afs_cell; buffer holds buffer_size bytes of a DNS server-list payload. Postcondition: returns a newly allocated afs_vlserver_list (caller owns the reference) or an ERR_PTR. A bad header (too short, wrong content type or version != 1) returns ERR_PTR(-EDESTADDRREQ); failure to allocate the list returns ERR_PTR(-ENOMEM). Otherwise it takes a reference on cell->vl_servers (under cell->vl_servers_lock) as 'previous' and parses each server record: a protocol other than unspecified/UDP gives -EPROTONOSUPPORT, an allocation failure -ENOMEM, an address-extraction error that error; each record reuses a matching server (same name, port, case-insensitive) from the previous list if present, replaces its address list when the new one is non-empty (under server->lock), skips records beyond nr_servers and records with no addresses when the server has none, and inserts the rest into vllist sorted by priority (lower first) then weight (higher first), clearing AFS_VLSERVER_FL_PROBED. If after the loop the cursor is not exactly at the end of the buffer (truncated record or trailing garbage) it fails; the errno then is the last value left in ret by the loop (-EPROTONOSUPPORT after a parsed record, or -ENOMEM if none). On success the previous-list reference is dropped and vllist returned; on any failure after allocation the new list, the previous-list reference and any server reference held are dropped and an ERR_PTR returned (a debug hex dump is printed unless the error is -ENOMEM).

name: afs_wait_for_vl_probes
prose: Real function int afs_wait_for_vl_probes(vllist, untried) in fs/afs/vl_probe.c (slice starts mid-function). Precondition: vllist is a valid VL server list with nr_servers <= BITS_PER_LONG, whose servers have probes started; untried is a bitmask of server indices to consider; the caller holds no lock. Postcondition: indices of servers whose AFS_VLSERVER_FL_PROBING is clear are dropped from the local mask; if any considered server already has AFS_VLSERVER_PROBE_RESPONDED, or no considered server remains, it returns 0 immediately without changing vllist->preferred. Otherwise it returns -ENOMEM if the wait-queue array cannot be allocated (nothing changed). Else it adds a wait entry on each considered server's probe_wq and sleeps interruptibly until any considered server has responded, or none is still probing, or a signal is pending; it then removes all wait entries, frees the array and, among the considered servers with AFS_VLSERVER_FL_RESPONDING, picks the one with the smallest rtt. If none responded and a signal is pending it returns -ERESTARTSYS; otherwise it sets vllist->preferred to the chosen index (when one exists, else leaves it unchanged) and returns 0.

name: afs_select_vlserver
prose: Precondition: vc was initialised by afs_begin_vlserver_operation; on calls after the first, vc->call_error and vc->call_abort_code hold the outcome of the previous call and vc->alist and vc->server_list hold the references acquired by earlier calls; single-threaded per cursor. Postcondition: increments vc->nr_iterations. Returns false immediately, touching nothing, if AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP is already set. On the first call it starts iteration (afs_start_vl_iteration: may wait for a DNS lookup; errors -ERESTARTSYS, -ENOENT, -EDESTADDRREQ recorded in cumul_error; an empty server list returns false without setting an error) and sends probes (error recorded and returns false). On later calls it first writes call_error to the used address's last_error and evaluates it: error 0 or an unlisted/local error: cumul_error.error = error, sets STOP and returns false, leaving vc->alist and vc->server_list references for afs_end_vlserver_operation to release; -ECONNABORTED with abort AFSVL_IO/BADVOLOPER/NOMEM moves to the next server, any other abort code is recorded (afs_prioritise_error) and the cursor fails; connection errors (-ERFKILL ... -ETIME) are recorded and the next address of the same server is tried; -ECONNRESET is recorded, sets AFS_VL_CURSOR_RETRY and goes to the next server; -EOPNOTSUPP goes to the next server. Server choice waits for probes (error from afs_wait_for_vl_probes recorded and fails) then picks the preferred untried server else the untried responding one with lowest rtt; if none are left it restarts once from the beginning when RETRY is set (dropping the old alist and server_list references; a second restart fails) or records the probe errors and fails. Returns true when an address has been selected: vc->server, vc->server_index and vc->alist (a reference to the server's address list, newly taken when the server changed) are set, vc->addr_index is the chosen untried responded address (preferred if available), that bit is set in vc->addr_tried and vc->call_responded is false. A false return after a failure also sets AFS_VL_CURSOR_STOP, drops the alist reference (updating alist->preferred if the last call responded on a different address) and leaves the server_list reference held for afs_end_vlserver_operation; the final error is in vc->cumul_error.

name: afs_create_volume
prose: Precondition: params is a valid mount request with params->cell, key, volname, volnamesz, type and force set; the caller holds no lock. Postcondition: looks up the VLDB entry by name (afs_vl_lookup_vldb) and returns an ERR_PTR on failure: -ERESTARTSYS if the VL operation could not begin, the negative error from afs_end_vlserver_operation (e.g. -EDESTADDRREQ) if no server answered, vldb->error if the VLDB query reported an error, -ENOMEDIUM if no suitable volume type exists (forced type not in vldb->flags; or neither RO nor RW is present), or the error from afs_lookup_volume (-ENOMEM or the server-list allocation error). When not forced, params->type is set to AFSVL_ROVOL if the VLDB has an RO volume, else AFSVL_RWVOL. On success it returns a volume of params->type: either a newly allocated candidate that was inserted into the cell and attached to its servers, or an existing live volume record for the same vid already in the cell (the new candidate is then put); in both cases the caller owns one reference and must release it with afs_put_volume. The fetched vldb entry is freed on every path after a successful VLDB lookup; no reference is taken on failure.

name: SYSCALL_DEFINE2(io_setup, unsigned, nr_events, aio_context_t __user *, ctxp)
prose: Generated syscall sys_io_setup(nr_events, ctxp). Precondition: ctxp is a user pointer to an aio_context_t slot; for success *ctxp must read as 0 and nr_events must be nonzero. Postcondition: returns -EFAULT (the get_user error) if *ctxp cannot be read, with nothing created; -EINVAL if *ctxp is nonzero or nr_events == 0; otherwise calls ioctx_alloc(nr_events) and, if that fails, returns its error (PTR_ERR; e.g. -EINVAL, -EAGAIN, -ENOMEM) with nothing created. On success it stores the new context's user_id into *ctxp with put_user: if that store succeeds it returns 0 and the context stays alive (owned by the process's ioctx table); if put_user fails it returns -EFAULT after killing the context via kill_ioctx(current->mm, ioctx, NULL). In both cases the temporary reference ioctx->users taken by ioctx_alloc is dropped (percpu_ref_put) before returning.

name: autofs_expire_wait
prose: Precondition: path->dentry is an autofs dentry with valid autofs_sb_info and autofs_info; the caller holds no sbi->fs_lock. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately if AUTOFS_INF_WANT_EXPIRE is not set in the dentry's autofs_info; if it is set and rcu_walk is nonzero it returns -ECHILD without waiting. Otherwise it loops under sbi->fs_lock: while the flags show only WANT_EXPIRE (an expire is being selected but not started) it drops the lock, sleeps HZ/10 uninterruptibly and re-checks; if the flags show AUTOFS_INF_EXPIRING it drops the lock, calls autofs_wait(sbi, path, NFY_NONE) (the status it returns is saved), then blocks on ino->expire_complete until the expire finishes, and returns -EAGAIN if the dentry is unhashed after the expire, otherwise returns that saved autofs_wait status (0, or e.g. -ENOENT, -EINTR, -ENOMEM, or the daemon-supplied status); if neither flag is set any longer it returns 0. fs_lock is not held on return; no reference is taken.

name: autofs_wait
prose: Precondition: sbi and path are valid, path->dentry is an autofs dentry, notify is NFY_MOUNT, NFY_EXPIRE or NFY_NONE, and the caller holds no sbi->wq_mutex. Postcondition: returns -ENOENT if sbi is catatonic, if the caller's pid or tgid cannot be translated into the daemon's pid namespace, if the dentry is negative and the mount is a trigger type or the parent is not the root, or if dentry_path_raw fails; -ENOMEM if the name buffer or wait-queue allocation fails; -EINTR if the interruptible lock of sbi->wq_mutex is interrupted. It then calls validate_request: if that returns <= 0 it is returned as is (0 means no wait is needed: the expire status is gone, or the mount point already has submounts; negative values are -ENOENT for catatonic or -EINTR) with the name buffer freed and wq_mutex released (not held when the error is -EINTR from relocking). Otherwise it joins an existing wait queue entry (wait_ctr incremented) or creates one (token assigned, linked into sbi->queues with wait_ctr 2, status preset to -EINTR) and has the daemon notified (autofs_notify_daemon, which releases wq_mutex), then sleeps killable until wq->name.name becomes NULL (released by the daemon or catatonic). It returns wq->status: the daemon-supplied status (0 on success), or -EINTR if the sleep was ended by a fatal signal before the daemon answered. When the status is 0 it records the requester's uid and gid in the dentry's autofs_info (or of its looked-up alias) under fs_lock. Finally it re-takes wq_mutex, decrements wq->wait_ctr, frees the wait-queue entry when the counter reaches zero, and releases the mutex; wq_mutex is not held on return.
